mainTopic: The ברכות the כהנים said in the מקדש, why the עשרת הדברות were dropped, whether a ברכה follows its ending, and the wording and bowing in the ברכות of שמע and תפילה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about the משנה in תמיד: was the single ברכה the כהנים said יוצר אור or אהבה רבה? The גמרא shows that because ריש לקיש's view was only inferred, his rule could be about the order of the ברכות, so nothing is proven. The משנה also says the כהנים read the עשרת הדברות. שמואל and a ברייתא of רבי נתן explain that this was stopped everywhere else because of the complaint of the מינים, and later חכמים who tried to bring it back were turned down. On שבת the outgoing משמר blessed the incoming one with love, brotherhood, peace and friendship. Back in our משנה, the גמרא asks what happens if a ברכה starts wrong but ends right, as when someone holds beer, thinks it is wine, and finishes with שהכל. Two proofs from a ברייתא ('everything follows the ending') are pushed off, so the question is never settled. The amud ends with רב's rulings: say אמת ויציב in the morning and אמת ואמונה at night, and in תפילה bow at ברוך and straighten up at ה׳'s name, which שמואל praised.

steps.title: Why the one blessing must have been יוצר אור
steps.stepSummary: If the כהנים had said אהבה רבה, the rule 'blessings do not hold each other back' could not be learned from this, because they might have simply waited to say יוצר אור until its proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say they said 'אהבה רבה', how would we learn that the blessings do not hold each other back? Maybe they skipped 'יוצר אור' only because its time had not come yet, and when the time came they said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the argument for how ריש לקיש's rule shows that the כהנים said יוצר אור and not אהבה רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they said יוצר אור and skipped אהבה רבה, the only reason for skipping it is that one ברכה is not needed for the other. If they said אהבה רבה and skipped יוצר אור, there is another simple reason: יוצר אור is about sunrise, and it was still too early. So only the יוצר אור version proves ריש לקיש's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'An abounding love', the second ברכה before שמע
'Who forms light', the first ברכה before שמע, about the morning light
They do not hold each other back; you can count one without the other

phrases.english: But if you say
that they would recite 'An abounding love',

phrases.aramaic: מַאי בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ?
phrases.english: what proof is there that the blessings do not hold each other back?
phrases.notes: He means that missing one ברכה doesn't stop the other one from counting.

phrases.english: Perhaps the fact that they did not say 'Who forms light'
was because the time for 'Who forms light' had not yet arrived,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מְטָא זְמַן ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי.
phrases.english: and when the time for 'Who forms light' arrived, they would say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי אָמְרַתְּ ״אַהֲבָה רַבָּה״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'אי אמרת בשלמא' argument begun just before this piece, which showed the יוצר אור reading fits ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.raayaObject: That the single ברכה said by the כהנים was יוצר אור
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's statement that ברכות אינן מעכבות זו את זו only makes sense if they said יוצר אור without אהבה רבה
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a later אמורא's rule can be used backwards to work out what an earlier משנה meant.

steps.title: So what if it was only an inference?
steps.stepSummary: The reasoning looks strong, so the גמרא asks what difference it makes that it was only inferred and not said outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was learned by inference, so what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יצחק בר יוסף bothered to point out that this was only an inference, since the inference seems solid. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the logic seemed to leave only one possible answer: יוצר אור. So calling it 'only an inference' seems to change nothing. The גמרא wants to know if an inference here is weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; worked out, not said directly
What? Here: so what difference does it make?

phrases.english: And if it was by inference, so what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the 'only by inference' label adds, given the strong reasoning of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference it makes that ריש לקיש's teaching about יוצר אור was only inferred and not stated outright

steps.title: An inference can be read differently: it may be about the order of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: If it was only an inference, maybe the כהנים said אהבה רבה, and later said יוצר אור when its time came. Then ריש לקיש's rule would only mean that the order of the ברכות does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it was by inference, really they said 'אהבה רבה', and when the time for 'יוצר אור' came they said it. And what does 'the blessings do not hold each other back' mean? The order of the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an inference can be broken. ריש לקיש's words could mean something else, so we cannot prove which ברכה the כהנים said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ריש לקיש had said outright 'they said יוצר אור', it would be settled. Because it was only worked out from his rule, we can read his rule differently: it is about saying the ברכות out of order (אהבה רבה first, יוצר אור later), not about skipping one. Read that way, the כהנים could have said אהבה רבה, and the proof for יוצר אור falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (a way of saying 'in truth it could be')

steps.whatToRemember: Because ריש לקיש's view was only inferred, ברכות אינן מעכבות זו את זו can be read as 'the order of the ברכות does not hold you back'. Then there is no proof that the כהנים said יוצר אור; they may have said אהבה רבה and added יוצר אור later.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this step says the ברכות may be skipped. In this reading, both ברכות are still said. The only thing that doesn't matter is which one comes first.

phrases.english: Because if it was by inference,
really they would recite 'An abounding love'.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מְטָא זְמַן ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: And when the time for 'Who forms light' arrived, they would say it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי ״בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ״
phrases.english: And what is meant by 'the blessings do not hold each other back'?
The order of the blessings.
phrases.notes: He means that saying them out of order still counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מִכְּלָלָא, לְעוֹלָם ״אַהֲבָה רַבָּה״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by showing that the inference in step 1 can be read another way.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since it was only inferred, ריש לקיש's rule could mean only that the order of the ברכות does not matter, so the כהנים may have said אהבה רבה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from ריש לקיש's rule that the single ברכה was יוצר אור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule can be read as being about order, not about skipping a ברכה, so it does not decide which ברכה was said
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why the גמרא cares whether a teaching was said outright or only inferred: an inference can be read another way.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the Ten Commandments and the other passages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the next line of the משנה in תמיד: the כהנים read the Ten Commandments, the three parts of שמע, אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they read the Ten Commandments, 'שמע', 'והיה אם שמוע', 'ויאמר', 'אמת ויציב', עבודה, and ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next part of the משנה so it can discuss it. This line sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having finished the question of which ברכה was said, the גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה. Something new is listed here: the כהנים also read the Ten Commandments before שמע. The next steps will ask what this means for everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The third part of שמע, about ציצית
'True and firm', the ברכה said after שמע in the morning
A ברכה about the Temple service (רצה)

phrases.english: And they read the Ten Commandments,
'Shema', 'VeHaya im Shamoa', 'VaYomer',
'True and Firm', Avoda, and the priestly benediction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the single ברכה and goes back to the משנה for its next line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the בית המקדש, the כהנים read the Ten Commandments together with the three parts of שמע, then said אמת ויציב, עבודה, and ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: שמואל: they wanted to say the Ten Commandments everywhere, but it was stopped
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: outside the מקדש they also wanted to say the עשרת הדברות daily, but it had already been stopped because of the complaint of the מינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Even outside the מקדש, people wanted to read the Ten Commandments this way. But it had already been stopped because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on the משנה it just quoted. שמואל explains why only the כהנים in the מקדש said the עשרת הדברות, and not everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in תמיד showed that the עשרת הדברות were part of the daily reading in the מקדש. שמואל adds that people elsewhere wanted to copy this, but it was cancelled. The reason was the complaint of the מינים. Commentators explain they would claim that only the עשרת הדברות came from God.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the עשרת הדברות are unimportant. The practice was stopped only so the heretics could not use it to back up their claim.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why we do not say the עשרת הדברות as part of our daily תפילה today.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Even in the outlying areas, they wanted to read this way,
phrases.notes: "This way" means reading the Ten Commandments every day, like the כהנים did in the משנה we just saw.

phrases.english: but they had already cancelled them
because of the complaint of the heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the practice in the משנה (saying the עשרת הדברות) was done only in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying the עשרת הדברות daily outside the מקדש was cancelled because of the complaint of the מינים.

steps.title: A ברייתא from רבי נתן says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי נתן says the same as שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: רבי נתן says: Outside the מקדש they wanted to read the Ten Commandments this way, but it had already been stopped because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up שמואל by showing that an earlier source, a ברייתא, says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "תניא נמי הכי" tells us no new idea is coming, only support. רבי נתן's words match שמואל's almost exactly, so שמואל's statement is confirmed by a תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (a supporting source)

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a ברייתא),
Rabbi Natan says:
In the outlying areas, they wanted to read this way,
but they had already cancelled them
because of the complaint of the heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's statement with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's statement that the daily reading of the עשרת הדברות was cancelled outside the מקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי נתן with the same words

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה wanted to bring it back in סורא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה wanted to set up the reading of the עשרת הדברות in סורא, but רב חסדא told him it had already been cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה thought to set up the reading of the Ten Commandments in סורא. רב חסדא told him: It was already cancelled because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of a later חכם who tried to bring the practice back, and was stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in a later generation, the cancellation still stood. רב חסדא answers with the exact words of the earlier rule, showing it was fixed and not to be changed.

keyTerms.meaning: To set them up as a fixed practice
A city in Babylonia with a big yeshiva

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana thought
to set them up in Sura,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the Ten Commandments, as part of the daily reading.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him:
They already cancelled them because of the complaint of the heretics.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה סְבַר לְמִקְבְּעִינְהוּ בְּסוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule from steps 5-6 being applied in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a later attempt to bring back the daily reading of the עשרת הדברות was blocked.

steps.title: אמימר wanted to bring it back in נהרדעא and was also stopped
steps.stepSummary: אמימר wanted to set up the reading in נהרדעא, and רב אשי told him the same thing: it was already cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר thought to set up the reading of the Ten Commandments in נהרדעא. רב אשי told him: It was already cancelled because of the complaint of the heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story with the same ending closes the topic: the cancellation stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This happened in a later generation and a different city, with the same answer. רב אשי repeats the very same words, which shows the rule was firm. The topic of the עשרת הדברות ends here.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים in the מקדש said the עשרת הדברות every day. Everywhere else this was cancelled because of the complaint of the מינים, and later attempts to bring it back were refused.

phrases.english: Ameimar thought
to set them up in Neharde'a,
Rav Ashi said to him:
They already cancelled them because of the complaint of the heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel story that confirms the outcome of step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The daily reading of the עשרת הדברות outside the מקדש stays cancelled because of the complaint of the מינים.

steps.title: On שבת one blessing is added for the outgoing watch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה in תמיד: on שבת the outgoing משמר gets one extra blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on שבת, they add one blessing for the outgoing priestly watch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next piece of the משנה in תמיד about the daily service of the כהנים. This is a setup line, because the next step asks what that blessing was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each week a new group of כהנים, a משמר, took over the מקדש service on שבת. The משנה says that on that day one extra blessing was said for the group that was leaving. It does not yet tell us the words.

keyTerms.meaning: A priestly watch, one of the groups of כהנים that took turns serving in the מקדש each week
The one going out, meaning the group finishing its week

phrases.english: And on Shabbat they add one blessing
for the outgoing priestly watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְשַׁבָּת מוֹסִיפִין בְּרָכָה אַחַת לַמִּשְׁמָר הַיּוֹצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה in תמיד that was brought in Step 4, after the side discussion about the עשרת הדברות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, one extra blessing is said for the outgoing משמר.

steps.title: What was that one blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what words made up the extra blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the one blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: what exactly did they say? This sets up רבי חלבו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said that a blessing was added and did not give its words. This is not an attack on the משנה. It is a request for missing information.

phrases.english: What is the one blessing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the blessing mentioned in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual words of the extra שבת blessing for the outgoing משמר.

steps.title: רבי חלבו gives the words of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו says the outgoing משמר blessed the incoming one with love, brotherhood, peace and friendship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: The outgoing watch says to the incoming watch: 'May He Who made His Name dwell in this House cause love, brotherhood, peace and friendship to dwell among you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו answers the question and gives us the exact words of the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A detail here is new: it is the outgoing group that blesses the incoming group. They pray that just as ה׳'s Name rests in the מקדש, love and peace should rest among the new group.

keyTerms.meaning: The one coming in, meaning the group starting its week

steps.whatToRemember: The extra שבת blessing was the outgoing כהנים blessing the incoming כהנים with love, brotherhood, peace and friendship.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said:
The outgoing watch says to the incoming watch:
'He Who caused His Name to dwell in this House,'
'may He cause to dwell among you'
'love and brotherhood and peace and friendship.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The outgoing משמר blesses the incoming משמר: 'May He Who made His Name dwell in this House make love, brotherhood, peace and friendship dwell among you.'

steps.title: Back to our משנה: where they said to make it long
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה in ברכות, which says a ברכה the חכמים made long may not be shortened.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A place where they said to make it long.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of תמיד and returns to our own משנה. This is a setup line for a new discussion about ending a ברכה with a different ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה taught that you must keep the form the חכמים set: a long ברכה may not be shortened, and a short one may not be made long. That rule shows that how a ברכה ends matters. The coming cases about wine and beer grow out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where they (the חכמים) said
To make long, meaning a ברכה that opens and closes with 'ברוך'

phrases.english: A place where they said to make it long.
phrases.notes: This is only the opening of the משנה's line. The rest says you may not shorten it, and a short ברכה may not be made long.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תמיד discussion and returns to the משנה in ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה the חכמים made long may not be shortened, and the reverse.

steps.title: Obvious case: wine he thought was beer
steps.stepSummary: If he holds wine, thinks it is beer, starts the ברכה with beer in mind and ends with the wine ending, he is obviously יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he holds a cup of wine, thinks it is beer, starts the blessing with beer in mind, and ends with the wine blessing, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: Before the real question, the גמרא gives an easy case it calls obvious: he started with beer in mind and finished with the correct wine ending. He is יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה on beer is שהכל and the ברכה on wine is בורא פרי הגפן. Here his drink really is wine, and he ended with the right ending for wine. The only issue is what was in his mind when he began.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine (its ברכה is בורא פרי הגפן)
With the intention of, with in mind

phrases.english: It is obvious: where he is holding
a cup of wine in his hand
and he thinks that it is beer,
and he opened and blessed with beer in mind,
phrases.notes: He said the opening, "ברוך אתה ה' אלוקינו מלך העולם", while planning to finish with the beer ending.

phrases.english: and he finished with the wine ending, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא הֵיכָא דְּקָא נָקֵיט כָּסָא דְחַמְרָא בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the theme of the משנה from Step 12 to set up an easy case before the hard one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine he mistook for beer: he started with beer in mind and ended with the wine ending, and he is יוצא.

steps.title: Why it's obvious: שהכל works for everything
steps.stepSummary: Even if he had finished with שהכל he would be יוצא, because a משנה says שהכל works for all foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because even if he had said 'that everything came to be by His word,' he would have fulfilled his obligation, as we learned: 'On all of them, if he said שהכל, he fulfilled his obligation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first case is obvious and brings a משנה as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the beer ברכה he first had in mind, שהכל, would work on wine after the fact. So starting with it in mind does not hurt him, and he also ended with the best ending. This is why the case is easy.

keyTerms.meaning: "That everything came to be by His word", the general ברכה
For we learned in a משנה
On all of them, meaning all foods and drinks

steps.confusionAlert: שהכל working on everything is only after the fact (בדיעבד). Ideally you still say the proper ברכה on each food.

phrases.english: For even if he had said
'that everything came to be by His word,' he would have fulfilled his obligation.
As we learned in a משנה:
On all of them, if he said
'that everything came to be by His word,' he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and the source for why Step 13 is obvious.
steps.raayaObject: That the wine case in Step 13 is obviously יוצא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: on all foods, if he said שהכל, he is יוצא.

steps.title: Real question: beer he thought was wine
steps.stepSummary: What if he holds beer, thinks it is wine, starts with wine in mind, and ends with the beer ending, שהכל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But where he is holding a cup of beer and thinks it is wine, he started the blessing with wine in mind and finished with the beer ending. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the real question, the reverse of the easy case. Here the start was wrong and the ending was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בורא פרי הגפן does not work on beer at all. So the part he began with wine in mind is wrong for this drink, while his ending, שהכל, is correct. Unlike the first case, that wrong start could make a real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: But, rather, introducing the real question
And he finished, he ended the ברכה

phrases.english: But where he is holding
a cup of beer in his hand
and he thinks that it is wine,
he opened and blessed with wine in mind,
and he finished with the beer ending, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּקָא נָקֵיט כָּסָא דְשִׁכְרָא בִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the easy case of Steps 13-14 around, to a case where the start was wrong and the ending was right.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is he יוצא if he started a ברכה with wine in mind over beer and ended with שהכל?

steps.title: Do we follow the main part or the ending?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the question in its sharpest form: does a ברכה follow its main part or its ending?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we go after the main part of the blessing, or do we go after the ending?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the question as a clear general rule: which part of a ברכה decides? The answer has not yet come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the main part (what he had in mind when he began) decides, he is not יוצא, since it was the wine ברכה over beer. If the ending decides, he is יוצא, since he ended with שהכל. The coming steps try to settle this.

keyTerms.meaning: The main part of the ברכה

steps.whatToRemember: The open question: when the start of a ברכה is wrong and the ending is right, does the main part decide, or the ending?
steps.whyThisMatters: This question about whether the main part or the ending of a ברכה decides affects any ברכה where the start and the ending do not match.

phrases.english: Do we go after the main part of the blessing,
phrases.notes: "Main part" means the start, when he had the wine ברכה in mind.

phrases.english: or do we go after the ending?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר עִיקַּר בְּרָכָה אָזְלִינַן אוֹ בָּתַר חֲתִימָה אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the question in Step 15 as a general rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of a ברכה decides whether it counts: its main part or its ending?

steps.title: A ברייתא about mixing up the morning and evening ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. In שחרית and in ערבית, if the ברכה before קריאת שמע ends wrong he is not יוצא, but if it starts wrong and ends right he is יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In the morning, if he began with 'Who creates light' and ended with 'Who brings on evenings,' he is not יוצא. If he began with 'Who brings on evenings' and ended with 'Who creates light,' he is יוצא. In the evening, if he began with 'Who brings on evenings' and ended with 'Who creates light,' he is not יוצא. If he began with 'Who creates light' and ended with 'Who brings on evenings,' he is יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question from Step 16. In every case, a correct ending is what makes the person יוצא, and a correct start alone is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא checks all four mix-ups: wrong start with a right ending, and right start with a wrong ending, for both שחרית and ערבית. Each time, the ending decides the outcome. This fits the beer case from Step 15, where he started with wine in mind but ended with the correct שהכל, so he should be יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who creates light': the morning ברכה before קריאת שמע
'Who brings on evenings': the evening ברכה before קריאת שמע
He fulfilled / did not fulfill his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: These are not ברכות of שמונה עשרה. They are the first ברכה before קריאת שמע, which is יוצר אור in the morning and מעריב ערבים at night.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In the morning prayer, if he began with 'Who creates light'
and ended with 'Who brings on evenings,' he is not יוצא.
If he began with 'Who brings on evenings'
and ended with 'Who creates light,' he is יוצא.
In the evening prayer, if he began with 'Who brings on evenings'
and ended with 'Who creates light,' he is not יוצא.
If he began with 'Who creates light'
and ended with 'Who brings on evenings,' he is יוצא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question asked in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That a ברכה follows its ending, so the beer case from Step 15 would be יוצא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about mixing up the endings of the ברכות before קריאת שמע in שחרית and ערבית.

steps.title: The rule: everything follows the ending
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up its cases with a general rule: everything follows the חתימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The general rule is: everything follows the ending.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states its general rule, and this is the line that seems to answer the question. If everything follows the ending, then in the beer case the ending שהכל should count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 gave single cases, and this line turns them into one clear rule. The rule answers Step 16 directly: a ברכה goes after its ending, not its main part. Taken at face value, the person in Step 15 would be יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter
The closing or ending of a ברכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This short line is the heart of the proof. The next step attacks it by asking whether it applies to every kind of ברכה.

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter is:
everything follows the ending.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from Step 17 by stating its general rule, which is the actual proof.
steps.raayaObject: A ברכה is decided by its ending.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The closing rule of the same ברייתא.

steps.title: Rejection: long ברכות with a separate closing are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברכות before קריאת שמע have a separate closing line that begins with ברוך, so their ending stands on its own. A short ברכה like שהכל has no separate closing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he says, 'Blessed are You, Who forms the lights.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. The ברייתא's rule may only apply to long ברכות that end with their own separate 'ברוך' line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יוצר אור there is a full closing ברכה, 'ברוך... יוצר המאורות,' so the ending counts as a complete ברכה by itself, even if the start was wrong. A short ברכה like שהכל or בורא פרי הגפן has no separate closing, so a mistake in its start may spoil the whole ברכה. Because of this, the question from Step 16 is not answered by this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: the case in the proof is not like our case
'Who forms the lights': the closing words of the morning ברכה

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that the ending decides only for long ברכות that have their own closing 'ברוך' line. For short ברכות like שהכל, the question from Step 16 is still open.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not argue with the rule 'everything follows the ending.' It only limits the rule to long ברכות with a separate closing, so the rule cannot be carried over to short ברכות.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since he says, 'Blessed... Who forms the lights.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Steps 17 and 18 by showing that the ברייתא's case is different from the beer case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא as proof for short ברכות on food and drink. The rule itself still holds for long ברכות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's ברכות have their own closing 'ברוך' line, so the ending counts by itself. Short ברכות like שהכל have nothing like that.

steps.title: Does the closing line really count as its own blessing for רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The rejection works for רב, since the closing line mentions God's name. For רבי יוחנן a ברכה needs מלכות, and the closing line has none, so it should not count as a separate ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רב, who says a ברכה without God's name is not a ברכה. The closing 'ברוך אתה ה׳ יוצר המאורות' has God's name, so it counts. But for רבי יוחנן, who says a ברכה without God's kingship is not a ברכה, what can we say? The closing line has no kingship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own rejection from Step 19. It says the idea that the closing line stands on its own only works for רב, not for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the closing line of the ברכות of קריאת שמע is a full ברכה by itself, so it can decide the ברכה even if the start was wrong. For רב that works, because the closing line says God's name. For רבי יוחנן a ברכה also needs מלכות ('מלך העולם'), which the closing line lacks. So it is not a separate ברכה, and the proof from Step 17 seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion)
What can we say? (there seems to be no answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question about wine and beer. It attacks the rejection in Step 19, which brings back the proof that everything follows the ending.

phrases.english: This works well for Rav, who said

phrases.aramaic: כָּל בְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם
phrases.english: any blessing that has no mention of God's name
is not a blessing. That is fine.
phrases.notes: The closing line 'ברוך אתה ה׳ יוצר המאורות' does say God's name, so for רב it counts.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said
any blessing that has no mention of God's kingship
is not a blessing, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 19 that the closing line of the ברכות of קריאת שמע is a separate ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יוחנן a ברכה needs מלכות. The closing line has none, so it is not a full ברכה by itself.

steps.title: The kingship said at the start covers both parts
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא said the ברכה mentions night in the day and day at night. So the name and kingship said at the start apply to both parts, and the ending is still a proper ברכה even for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר עולא said the ברכה mentions the quality of day at night and the quality of night in the day. Since that is so, when one says God's name and kingship at the start, he says them for both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge, so the rejection from Step 19 still stands. The kingship at the opening of the ברכה counts for the ending too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the morning we say 'יוצר אור ובורא חשך', which mentions darkness by day. At night we say 'גולל אור מפני חשך', which mentions light at night. Because each ברכה covers both day and night, the opening kingship applies to the whole ברכה. So for רבי יוחנן the ending can also act as a full ברכה, and there is still no proof for a short ברכה like שהכל.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא:
phrases.english: Rather, since Rabba bar Ulla said:
in order to mention the quality of day at night
and the quality of night in the day,
phrases.notes: He means the morning ברכה says 'ובורא חשך', so darkness is mentioned by day.

phrases.english: when he says God's name and kingship at the start
he is saying it for both of them.
phrases.notes: Both day and night, so the opening kingship carries over to the ending too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 and keeps the rejection of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the opening kingship covers the whole ברכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The closing line has no מלכות, so for רבי יוחנן it is not a separate ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opening מלכות applies to both parts, so the ending is a proper ברכה even for רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A new proof from the general rule of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with 'the general rule: everything follows the ending'. A general rule should add a new case, maybe our case of a short ברכה like שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the end of the ברייתא: 'The general rule is: everything follows the ending.' What does 'the general rule' come to include? Doesn't it come to include our case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for its question. It looks at the extra words 'the general rule' at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא that adds a 'general rule' after its cases is usually including something more. The גמרא suggests the extra case is ours: even a short ברכה like שהכל follows its ending. If so, the man who ended with שהכל would be יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a teaching
The general rule of the matter

phrases.english: Come and hear from the end part:
"The general rule of the matter:
everything follows the ending."
"The general rule": what does it come to include?
Doesn't it come to include what we said?
phrases.notes: Our case: a short ברכה that started with wine in mind and ended with שהכל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a second proof from the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That even a short ברכה follows its ending.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'כללו של דבר' at the end of the ברייתא.

steps.title: No, the rule adds a case of bread and dates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The general rule may be adding a case about bread and dates, not our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it comes to include a case of bread and dates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by giving a different case that 'the general rule' could include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the extra words can include a different case, they do not prove anything about our question. The גמרא offers bread and dates as that other case. The next step asks what exactly that case is.

phrases.english: No, it comes to include bread and dates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from 'כללו של דבר'. The question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The general rule could be including a different case, bread and dates.

steps.title: What is the bread-and-dates case? Not one that is just our question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the bread-and-dates case is. If it means he ate bread, thought it was dates, began the dates ברכה and ended with the bread ending, that is exactly our open question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he ate bread and thought he was eating dates, began the ברכה with dates in mind and ended with the bread ending, that is our very question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the rejection by asking what the bread-and-dates case could be. It rules out the first option, since that would just be our question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first option has the same pattern as the wine-and-beer case: the start was wrong and the ending was right. The rejection cannot use a case that is the very thing we are unsure about. So the גמרא will need a different explanation of the bread-and-dates case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (an option about to be rejected)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say he ate bread,
and thought he was eating dates,
and began the blessing with dates in mind
and ended with the ending for bread
that is our very question!
phrases.notes: It has the same pattern as the wine-and-beer question in Step 15: a wrong start and a right ending.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rejection in Step 23 by defining its case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 23 that the general rule includes bread and dates.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The simple version of the bread-and-dates case is the same as our open question, so it cannot be a separate case.

steps.title: The bread-and-dates case is the reverse case
steps.stepSummary: The general rule is about someone who ate dates, thought they were bread, and began with the bread ברכה. He is יוצא, because even ending with bread's ending would have worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed for this case: he ate dates but thought he ate bread. He opened with the bread ברכה and closed with the dates ברכה, and he is יוצא. That is because even if he had closed with the bread ending, he would also be יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24 by flipping the case around. Here he ate dates, not bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the 'wrong' opening, the bread ברכה, is not really wrong for dates, because it would work even as a full ברכה. So nothing here was truly said in error. That is why this case does not answer our open question about a ברכה with a truly wrong opening.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (only) for... A phrase that brings in the specific case a rule is really about

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction! In step 24 he ate bread and thought it was dates. Here he ate dates and thought it was bread. That flip is the whole answer.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a case where he ate dates,
and he thought he ate bread,
and he opened with the bread blessing,
and ended with the dates blessing: he has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: For even if he had ended with the bread blessing, he would also have fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24's question by defining the bread-and-dates case as the reverse case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bread-and-dates case seemed to be our open question: a wrong opening with a right ending.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is dates mistaken for bread, where the bread opening is valid anyway. So it proves nothing about a truly wrong opening.

steps.title: Why would the bread ending work for dates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the bread ברכה would count for dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the claim it just made. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 claimed that ending with the bread ברכה would work for dates. That is surprising, since dates normally get a different ברכה. So the גמרא wants the reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 25's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the bread ברכה would be valid after the fact for dates.

steps.title: Because dates also nourish
steps.stepSummary: Dates also give nourishment, so the bread ברכה (הזן) still fits them after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because dates also nourish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that dates are filling food too, so a bread ברכה is not a mistake for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread ברכה praises God for food that sustains, and dates fit that description. So after the fact he is יוצא. This is exactly why the case does not answer our open question about a truly wrong opening, which is left unresolved.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'general rule' (follow the ending) teaches the dates-thought-to-be-bread case. Our question about a wrong opening with a right ending is not settled by it.

phrases.english: Because dates also nourish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dates are sustaining food, so the bread ברכה is valid for them after the fact.

steps.title: Saying אמת ויציב in the morning and אמת ואמונה at night
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא in the name of רב: if you did not say אמת ויציב in שחרית and אמת ואמונה in ערבית, you are not יוצא. The source is a פסוק that pairs kindness with morning and faithfulness with night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: Anyone who did not say 'אמת ויציב' in the morning and 'אמת ואמונה' in the evening has not fulfilled his obligation. As it says: 'To tell of Your kindness in the morning, and Your faithfulness at night.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the wording of the ברכה after קריאת שמע, which must differ between morning and night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time of day has its own opening words, and saying the wrong one means you are not יוצא. The פסוק links morning with חסד (kindness) and night with אמונה (faithfulness). That is why the night version uses the word אמונה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'True and firm': the morning ברכה after שמע
'True and faithful': the evening ברכה after שמע

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the different morning and evening wording of the ברכה of redemption (גאולה) after שמע.

phrases.english: Rabbah bar Chinnana the Elder said
in the name of Rav:
Anyone who did not say 'True and Firm' in the morning,
and 'True and Faithful' in the evening,
has not fulfilled his obligation,
as it is said: 'To tell of Your kindness in the morning,'
'and Your faithfulness at night.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the wording of the ברכות of קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the morning you must say אמת ויציב, and at night אמת ואמונה. Otherwise you are not יוצא.

steps.title: When to bow and when to stand up in תפילה
steps.stepSummary: Another ruling from the same speaker: in תפילה you bow at the word ברוך and straighten up at God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: One who prays, when he bows, he bows at 'ברוך', and when he straightens up, he straightens up at God's name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from the same speaker, this time about how to bow during the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bow matches the words: you bend down when saying 'ברוך' (Blessed) and are already upright by the time you say God's name. This gives the exact timing for the bows.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא [סָבָא] מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: And Rabbah bar Chinnana the Elder said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: One who prays, when he bows,
bows at 'Blessed',
and when he straightens up, he straightens up at the Name.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same speaker, on a new subject (bowing in תפילה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bow at 'ברוך' and straighten up at God's name.

steps.title: שמואל gives the source for straightening up at ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains רב's ruling using the פסוק 'ה׳ זוקף כפופים‎'. ה׳ straightens the bent, so we straighten up when we say His name.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: What is רב's reason? Because it is written: 'ה׳ straightens those who are bent over.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a פסוק as the reason for רב's ruling from step 29, that you straighten up at ה׳'s name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes ה׳ as the One who straightens the bent. So when a person who is bowing reaches ה׳'s name, he straightens up. His body acts out the פסוק.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: What is Rav's reason?
As it is written: "ה׳ straightens those who are bent over."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רב's ruling in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that one straightens up at ה׳'s name

steps.title: A פסוק seems to say we should be bowed at ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges with the פסוק 'מפני שמי נחת הוא'. It seems to say a person should be humbled, meaning bowed, at ה׳'s name.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'Before My name he was humbled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea of standing straight at ה׳'s name. It uses a פסוק that praises someone for being humbled before that name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being humbled before ה׳'s name is praiseworthy, then it seems you should be bowing at the name, not straightening up. That clashes with רב's ruling and with שמואל's source.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, raising a difficulty from a source
Was humbled or afraid, brought low

phrases.english: They challenged:
"Before My name he was humbled."
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:5. The פסוק is praising the כהן for this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling and source from steps 29 and 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling to straighten up at ה׳'s name
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק praises being humbled before ה׳'s name, which suggests bowing at the name rather than straightening.

steps.title: 'Before My name' means bowing before the name, at ברוך
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'מפני שמי', before My name, not 'בשמי', at My name. So the bowing happens before the name is said, at ברוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'at My name'? It says 'before My name'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the exact words of the פסוק carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Before' means earlier in time, before the name comes. So the פסוק fits רב perfectly. You bow at ברוך, which comes before the name, and straighten up at the name itself.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'מפני' here as 'because of'. The answer depends on reading it as 'before', earlier than the name is said.

phrases.english: Is it written "at My name"?
"Before My name" is written.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to require bowing at ה׳'s name.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק requires humbling before the name, meaning at ברוך. At the name itself one straightens up, as רב said.

steps.title: שמואל praises רב's ruling to רב's son
steps.stepSummary: שמואל calls חייא בר רב a 'son of Torah' and repeats his father's fine ruling: bow at ברוך, straighten up at the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to חייא בר רב: Son of Torah, come and I will tell you a fine saying of your father. Your father said: When one bows, he bows at 'ברוך'. When he straightens up, he straightens up at the Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. שמואל tells רב's son how great his father's ruling was, and the ruling is repeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the challenge is answered, the ruling stands firm. שמואל, רב's colleague, calls it 'a fine saying'. That shows he fully agreed with it and valued it.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of Torah, a term of praise

steps.whatToRemember: In תפילה you bow when you say ברוך and straighten up by the time you say ה׳'s name. The source is 'ה׳ זוקף כפופים', and 'מפני שמי' means bowing before the name.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב:
phrases.english: Shmuel said to Chiyya, son of Rav:
Son of Torah,
come and I will tell you
a fine saying that your father said.
This is what your father said:
When one bows, he bows at "Baruch,"
and when he straightens up, he straightens up at the Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge is answered, the גמרא closes by repeating רב's ruling, praised by שמואל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Bow at ברוך and straighten up at ה׳'s name. שמואל considered this an especially fine ruling.
